text:
sam: Quick heads-up — pushed a runtime cleanup PR that removes the legacy per-request allocator cache. PR: https://git.redwood/ri/runtime/pull/842 (please don't merge automatically). Observed a small throughput dip on longseq benchmark, might affect the 16:00 PT canary. Need quick eyes + opinion on merge timing.

linh: looking now

jordan: can you paste the bench output you saw?

sam: pasted below from local perf rig:
```
Benchmark: longseq-16k tokens
Before (main): throughput 2100 tok/s, p95 120ms, p99 220ms, mem 12.1GB
After (cleanup): throughput 1987 tok/s (-5.3%), p95 125ms, p99 225ms, mem 12.4GB (+300MB)
Commit: 8a3f2c4 remove-legacy-alloc-cache
```

linh: hmm 300MB peak and a throughput hit. did the cleanup change any memcpy/pathing?

sam: it collapses one small cache layer; that should reduce frag long-term but it exposes an extra copy in the hot path for small requests. suspect the memcpy cost + allocation churn on p3-small.

marta: is this visible on canary images? Hosted traffic is tail-sensitive so even modest throughput regressions matter.

jordan: i ran the microbench on a canary-like node image (kernel 5.10) and the throughput drop is ~2% there, not 5%. on older nodes (kernel 5.4) it's ~5%. p99/tail stayed within noise. so kernel interaction likely.

alex: do we have CI/bench gating? @devbot any updates on the bench-suite run for this PR?

devbot: CI: unit tests ✅, integration tests: 5/12 running, bench-suite job queued (priority: medium). See CI: https://ci.redwood/842

sam: options: (A) revert cleanup and keep old perf, (B) add a conditional to use old allocator on kernels <= 5.4, (C) micro-optim the memcpy path (probably small win). What do folks prefer given canary at 16:00 PT?

jordan: my take — for Hosted we prefer throughput. If the cleanup is correctness/maintenance-only, defer it and keep canary. If the cleanup fixes a correctness bug, we need to merge but gate it behind canary+fallback.

linh: i can approve after a follow-up patch that removes the extra memcpy (should be a ~15-30m change). If sam can push that quick, i'm OK.

marta: agreed — avoid merging a regression before canary unless we have a fallback policy. If we do merge, schedule a canary with auto-fallback to model-var-B for 2h and a rollback trigger on p95 > +10% or mem +500MB.

alex: +1 to adding a smoke check in the canary job that runs the longseq-1k/16k quick bench and asserts p95 and mem thresholds.

sam: i'll work on the memcpy patch and push it in ~30m, then request final approvals. i'll also add the canary smoke test if we need to roll forward. thanks all.

devbot: update: integration tests passed (12/12), bench-suite started (estimating ~18m).

jordan: sounds good. tagging for approvals: @linh @alex @marta — please ack once you see the patch.

linh: ack after patch

alex: ack

marta: ack if canary + fallback configured :thumbsup:

sam: noted, will post another ping when patch pushed.
